clue.text: Fruit and vegetables for Mussolini

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in arguments pro and con
Mussolini styled himself Il Duce, the leader

explanation.surface: A request for fresh food to be sent to the Italian dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'for' someone is being pro them; Mussolini's title was Il Duce.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce is the collective grocer's word for farm-grown fruit and vegetables.

clue.text: Old man gets pastries from opium producers

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, one's old man
pies are baked pastry dishes

explanation.surface: A father collects baked goods from drug growers.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is extracted from the seed heads of a species of poppy flower.

clue.text: Manage to describe episcopal status

definitions.meaning: to supervise or run something
a bishop is placed above, or in charge of, his see, his diocese

explanation.surface: A question of how to put a bishop's rank into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to manage; and a bishop sits over a see, his diocese, split as two words.

clue.text: Unexpected reversal for top people

definitions.meaning: a surprise defeat of a favourite, as in a sporting shock
the upper set, people at the top of society

explanation.surface: A sudden turnaround in fortune for the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock result is an upset; split as two words it describes a high social set.

clue.text: Charming conclusion to each operatic cycle

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
Wagner's four-opera cycle is known as the Ring

explanation.surface: A delightful finale to every opera sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ring, short for Der Ring des Nibelungen, is Wagner's cycle of four operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Endearing behaviour inspires affection, as charming behaviour does.

clue.text: One who jeers Billy Bunter, for instance

definitions.meaning: a person who mocks or derides
Billy Bunter is the greedy fat schoolboy of the Greyfriars stories, forever gobbling food

explanation.surface: Someone mocking the famous fat boy of school stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a gluttonous schoolboy from classic British children's stories; to scoff is also to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is both to mock and, in British slang, to wolf down food.

clue.text: Make a declaration to the nation

definitions.meaning: to announce or assert formally
a country with its own government

explanation.surface: Making a public announcement to the whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to state; a country or polity is a state.

clue.text: Extensive picnic

definitions.meaning: spread wide, broad in extent
a meal laid out in the open air

explanation.surface: A lavish outdoor meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretched wide is extensive; a picnic is literally a spread set outdoors.

clue.text: Well off local paper nothing but a hotchpotch

parts.note: far off, a long way away, as 'well off course'
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The local newspaper, far from good, is merely a jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well off' tempts as wealthy, but it means far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble, a mixture just like a hotchpotch.

clue.text: Ignorant farm-worker has a ruddy cheek

parts.note: ruddy means red-faced
neck is old British slang for cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: A rustic labourer with a sunburnt face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' is not the face but impudence, also called neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Redneck is a derogatory term for an unsophisticated rural labourer.

clue.text: Gratified by urgent requests to receive education

parts.note: pleas are earnest appeals

explanation.surface: Someone made happy by fervent appeals to be taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To receive' simply has the pleas take the abbreviation on their end.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gratified is to be satisfied or delighted.

clue.text: Territorials withdraw exhausted, but in proper array

indicators.note: to withdraw is to draw back, so the Territorials' letters go backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army
tired means worn out

explanation.surface: Weary part-time soldiers retreat, yet still smartly turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdraw' reads the Territorial Army's two letters backwards; TA is the British volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Attired means dressed, so arrayed in proper clothing.

clue.text: Popular week-end tea I prepare if inordinately hungry

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Sat, Saturday, is part of the weekend

indicators.note: to prepare is to make ready by arranging, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A trendy weekend cuppa I make when I am ravenous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepare' rearranges the letters of 'tea I'; the weekend's first day is abbreviated as part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiate is a literary word for never satisfied, so endlessly greedy.

clue.text: No aggression at all in a top-class sportsman

annotationWithheld.why: No aggression at all in a top-class sportsman: ACE is the top-class sportsman but no clue word gives the remaining PE, so the clue looks garbled as held.
annotationWithheld.clue: No aggression at all in a top-class sportsman

clue.text: Wrote down the letters of wheat'

definitions.meaning: spelled out a word letter by letter
an ancient variety of wheat

explanation.surface: Someone spelled out the name of a cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is the British past tense of spell, and also an old kind of grain.

clue.text: Pitch Peter's pal in a canvas sheet

parts.note: pitch is black tar
the apostles Peter and Paul are paired, as in robbing Peter to pay Paul

explanation.surface: Throwing Peter's friend into a tent cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof cover of tarred canvas.

clue.text: On trial for harbouring

definitions.meaning: the accused stands in a box in a criminal court
a ship berthed at a quay is kept in port

explanation.surface: Someone facing charges for sheltering a fugitive.
explanation.definitionFit: The accused stands in a court enclosure on trial; a ship moored in harbour sits in its berth.

clue.text: Hawking includes everything in a summing-up

indicators.note: includes means one word holds another inside it here

parts.note: toting means carrying or peddling, as a hawker does
all means everything

explanation.surface: The physicist Hawking taking in the whole story in a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawking' reads as the physicist but means peddling goods about; 'includes' signals that one word sits inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalling is adding up figures, a summing-up.

clue.text: Blunt battle-cry of militant Socialists

definitions.meaning: frank, straightforward, outright
left-wingers might chant for the Right to be brought down

explanation.surface: A frank slogan shouted by left-wing radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means utterly plain and outspoken; split, it is a shout against the political Right.

clue.text: Knotty Ash comedian he si tates and founders

parts.note: Ken Dodd, the British comic, came from Knotty Ash in Liverpool
says er, er, as one does when hesitating

explanation.surface: A Liverpool comic stammers and then collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian from Knotty Ash, Liverpool; one who hesitates 'ers'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to totter shakily, stumbling as one who founders does.

clue.text: How retrievers celebrate retrieving a bird

definitions.meaning: a dog pleased after fetching shakes its rear appendage
a small long-tailed songbird of the genus Motacilla

explanation.surface: Gun dogs show delight on bringing back game.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs show joy by shaking their tails; it is also the name of a common bird.

clue.text: He bowled over Medina- Sidonia

parts.note: the English admiral famed for finishing his game of bowls before defeating the Armada led by the Duke of Medina-Sidonia

explanation.surface: A man knocked over a Spanish duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Sir Francis Drake played bowls on Plymouth Hoe before beating the Spanish Armada, commanded by the Duke of Medina-Sidonia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan seaman both played bowls and overcame the Armada's admiral.

clue.text: Pickled caviare exemplifies greed

indicators.note: pickled suggests something altered or in a mess, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Preserved fish roe shows gluttony.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, a form of greed.

clue.text: Immortal description of Schubert's Eighth

definitions.meaning: living for ever
Schubert's Eighth Symphony is the Unfinished, so it has no conclusion

explanation.surface: Praise for a deathless symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immortal never stops; the Unfinished Symphony literally lacks its close.

clue.text: Arrogant assertion of belief in Romulus' lupine nurse

definitions.meaning: a doctrine laid down as beyond question
Romulus was suckled by a she-wolf, a dog-mother

explanation.surface: Faith in the wolf that reared Rome's founder.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend Romulus and Remus were nursed by a she-wolf; read as DOG MA, a canine mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a creed laid down as incontrovertibly true.

clue.text: Pension for all the trustees

definitions.meaning: a pension is a boarding house, where meals are included
the entire board of trustees

explanation.surface: Retirement income for every member of a trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' tempts as retirement income but is the French boarding-house sense, as in full pension with all meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Full board means lodging with all meals; split, it is the complete governing committee.

clue.text: Sweet waffle

definitions.meaning: a soft confection
to evade, talk vaguely

explanation.surface: A dessert of batter cooked in a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection, and to fudge an issue is to evade it with vague talk.

clue.text: Make Rex enter an orchestra

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the king goes inside the orchestra

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Forcing a king to join a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a make, the name a manufacturer sells under.

clue.text: Made it possible for Eugenia to get a phlebotomy

parts.note: Princess Victoria Eugenie, later Queen of Spain, was known as Ena
phlebotomy is drawing blood, so the person bled

explanation.surface: A woman submits to a blood test.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Eugenie of Battenberg, Queen of Spain, was known as Ena; ENA is a pet form of Eugenia.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to make something possible.

clue.text: Quite crazy about Light Infantry all dressed up like soldiers

indicators.note: about means round, so the crazy word goes around the infantry

parts.note: inane means senseless, absurd
LI is the military abbreviation for Light Infantry

explanation.surface: Absurd soldiers in uniform parade together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' is the drill sense: soldiers dressed are lined up straight. 'about' signals that the crazy word wraps the regiment's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops dressed by the right stand in a straight row, aligned.

clue.text: Not a whisper!

parts.note: a command for total hush, not even a murmur

explanation.definitionFit: Total quiet means not even a murmur is heard.

clue.text: Traipses around to procure gimmicky appliances

indicators.note: around means one word encircles the other here

parts.note: gads means wanders about idly
get means obtain

explanation.surface: Wandering about to buy novelty kitchenware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traipses' is the wandering sense of gadding about; 'around' signals that it wraps the word for procure.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgets are small ingenious devices, often gimmicks.
